correctness.rationale: Singleton traces imply every edge has a leaf endpoint, giving a star forest. For a star of s edges, a proper nonempty trace of size t requires t leaves and the full trace costs one hub; the maximum cost is max(1,s-1). The empty trace forces r outside vertices. Selecting cost-minimizing vertices in each component and padding externally proves iff. For k edges and m star components, minimum possible cost is max(m,k-m); minimizing m under this and the support bound yields the exact dimension min(2r,n-r-1,floor(n/2)), truncated at zero. Explicit labeled component counts produce the triangular shattering polynomial. The actual verify.py passes all n<=6 edge subsets, bounded-size n=7,8, and exact triangular counts n<=8.

value.rationale: Fixed-cardinality witness constraints change an unrestricted star-forest result into a sharp resource-budget theorem with a nontrivial phase diagram VC=min(2r,n-r-1,floor(n/2)). The exact classified r=2 spectrum shows a real open-versus-closed threshold shift in triangular Johnson graphs and counts every shattered subset type. These are natural learning-theoretic and finite-model invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices.
